Fishbot_Depth_Threshold_Check

2026-10-21

Motivation

This analysis is intended to take a deeper look at the differences between the entire FIShBOT dataset under two depth filters. The first filter has a 20m ceiling and the second data set has a 10 meter ceiling.

library(sf)
library(ncdf4)

terra::terraOptions(progress = 0)
# Load FIShBOT standardized 7km grid (geopackage)
botgrid <- terra::vect('botgrid.gpkg')
names(botgrid)[1] <- 'grid_id'
#terra::crs(botgrid, describe = TRUE)

# # Get Bathy 
# bathy <- marmap::getNOAA.bathy(-78,-64, 33, 46)
# #bathy <- terra::rast(marmap::as.raster(bathy))
# bathy_mat <- (as.matrix(bathy))
# bathy <- terra::rast(bathy_mat, 
#                      ext = terra::ext(-78, -64, 33, 46), 
#                      crs = "EPSG:4326")
# bathy <- terra::t(bathy)
# bathy <- terra::flip(bathy, direction = "vertical")

# Load NES Map
load('nes_map.Rdata')
bathy <- terra::rast(bathy)
terra::crs(bathy) <- 'EPSG:4326'
us.vect <- terra::vect(sf::st_as_sf(us.coast))
#crs(us.vect)

# Pull in the 10 m filtered raster w/out gliders
temp_stack_10m <- terra::rast('temp_stack_10m.tif')
sal_stack_10m <- terra::rast('sal_stack_10m.tif')

# Pull in the 20 m filtered raster w/out gliders
temp_stack_20m <- terra::rast('temp_stack_20m.tif')
sal_stack_20m <- terra::rast('sal_stack_20m.tif')
## ---- Calc differences ------ ##
terra::terraOptions(progress = 0)
# Temperature
# Take diff between 20 meter and 10 meter cap (on filtered raster w/out gliders)
diff_rast <- temp_stack_20m - temp_stack_10m
# do this now bc it keeps breaking down below
bathy_utm <- terra::project(bathy, terra::crs(diff_rast))

# set up for MAE and RMSE 
abs_rast_temp  <- abs(diff_rast) # mae mean of abs vals
sq_rast_temp   <- (diff_rast)^2    # rmse mean of sqrt

mae_values  <- terra::global(abs_rast_temp, fun = "mean", na.rm = TRUE)
rmse_values <- terra::global(sq_rast_temp, fun = "mean", na.rm = TRUE)
mean_values <- terra::global(diff_rast, fun = 'mean', na.rm = TRUE)
valid_cells <- terra::global(!is.na(diff_rast), fun="sum")
 
daily_stats <- data.frame(
  Layer_Index = 1:terra::nlyr(temp_stack_20m), # Keeps track of which layer
  Day         = names(temp_stack_20m),
  ME          = mean_values[, 1],
  MAE         = mae_values[, 1],
  RMSE        = sqrt(rmse_values[, 1]), 
  Valid       = valid_cells[,1]
)

# Salinity 
diff_rast_sal <-  sal_stack_20m - sal_stack_10m
# set up for MAE and RMSE 
abs_rast_sal  <- abs(diff_rast_sal) # mae mean of abs vals
sq_rast_sal   <- (diff_rast_sal)^2    # rmse mean of sqrt

mae_values_sal  <- terra::global(abs_rast_sal, fun = "mean", na.rm = TRUE)
rmse_values_sal <- terra::global(sq_rast_sal, fun = "mean", na.rm = TRUE)
mean_values_sal <- terra::global(diff_rast_sal, fun = 'mean', na.rm = TRUE)
valid_cells <- terra::global(!is.na(diff_rast_sal), fun="sum")

daily_stats_sal <- data.frame(
  Layer_Index = 1:terra::nlyr(sal_stack_20m), # Keeps track of which layer to plot
  Day         = names(sal_stack_20m),
  ME          = mean_values_sal[, 1],
  MAE         = mae_values_sal[, 1],
  RMSE        = sqrt(rmse_values_sal[, 1]), 
  Valid       = valid_cells[,1]
)

Temperature

Isolating the top 50 days that had the highest RMSE, then looking at how those days are spread out across years and months to see if there are any systemic annual or seasonal biases.

# Temperature 
# Isolate top days with/highest RMSE
top_error_days <- daily_stats[order(-daily_stats$RMSE), ][1:10, ]
top_50_error_days <- daily_stats[order(-daily_stats$RMSE), ][1:50, ]
top_50_error_days <- top_50_error_days |> 
  dplyr::mutate(Date = lubridate::ymd(Day), 
                Year = lubridate::year(Date), 
                Month = lubridate::month(Date), 
                Month.fac = lubridate::month(Date, label = TRUE, 
                                             abbr = TRUE))
# length(sort(unique(top_50_error_days$Year)))
# length(sort(unique(top_50_error_days$Month)))
top_error_days      
##      Layer_Index        Day          ME       MAE      RMSE Valid
## 6061        6061 2020-07-19  0.27088447 0.3246806 1.3998579    22
## 2247        2247 2009-08-25  0.31631580 0.3163158 0.9749508    19
## 3491        3491 2013-07-05  0.33026568 0.3338355 0.9297079    24
## 6063        6063 2020-07-21  0.12234660 0.1285315 0.6985113    31
## 154          154 2000-10-05 -0.16411764 0.1641176 0.6766744    17
## 5938        5938 2020-03-18 -0.12719830 0.1271983 0.6359915    25
## 4622        4622 2016-08-10 -0.10959811 0.1112061 0.5059362    21
## 6054        6054 2020-07-12  0.09505491 0.1021345 0.4626428    22
## 5700        5700 2019-07-24  0.10235139 0.1088653 0.4343540    28
## 3252        3252 2012-09-01 -0.09693374 0.1057233 0.4300712    18
  • Years represented: N = 19
  • Months represented: N = 12

While all 12 months are represented in the top 50 highest error days, their spread is not distributed evenly. The summer months of July and August hold the majority of highest errors, with roughly 18 of the 50 highest errors days. The spring and fall have the next highest error rate. Could this be a signal of stratification, which is highest in summer?

hist(top_50_error_days$Month)

barplot(table(top_50_error_days$Month.fac), 
        main = 'Distribution of Top 50 Error Days by Month: Temperature',
        xlab = 'Month', 
        ylab = 'Frequency',
        ylim = c(0,10),
        col = 'steelblue', 
        border = 'black',
        las = 1)

  • Range of MAE: 0.0424969, 0.3338355
  • Range of RMSE: 0.1882307, 1.3998579

The average temperature discrepancy (MAE) between the 20m vs 10m cap does not exceed 0.333°C for any given day across the whole data set. That MAE is only realized on 3 occasions and falls quickly to 0.1°C for the remaining top 10 error days. This level of difference seems reasonable, considering most sensors have precision limits around ±0.1°C to ±0.2°C. While the RMSE range suggests some areas where the differences are quite large, the low MAE confirms those are localized spikes.

Salinity

# Isolate top days with/highest RMSE
top_error_days_sal <- daily_stats_sal[order(-daily_stats_sal$RMSE), ][1:10, ]
top_50_error_days_sal <- daily_stats_sal[order(-daily_stats_sal$RMSE), ][1:50, ]

  • Months represented: N = 0

Summer and fall (Aug, Oct) represent the highest mismatch in salinities at 20 vs 10m depths. This is not surprising again - stratification and also highly dynamic times of year in our region. Still with the majority of MAEs lower than 0.2 its likely the few instances of higher discrepancies are localized.

hist(top_50_error_days_sal$Month)

barplot(table(top_50_error_days_sal$Month.fac), 
        main = 'Distribution of Top 50 Error Days by Month: Salinity',
        xlab = 'Month', 
        ylab = 'Frequency',
        ylim = c(0,15),
        col = 'brown', 
        border = 'black',
        las = 1) 

# range(top_50_error_days_sal$MAE)
# range(top_50_error_days_sal$RMSE)

The maximum MAE for salinity between the 20m vs 10m cap is 0.093 and the minimum is one-thousandth of a psu. An average difference ~0.1 in salinity can be meaningful, however this only occurs on one instance across all days and quickly drops to errors between 0.02-0.04.

  • Range of MAE: 0.1021345, 0.3338355
  • Range of RMSE: 0.4300712, 1.3998579

Temperature & Salinity x Year

A look at errors across years - no clear pattern across datasets.

The temperature figure cluster has a cluster of higher errors in 2018-2020. These were warm years in the ocean, maybe highly stratified or dynamic? For instance, 2018 had greater than 35 WCRs Gangopadhyay et al. 2020.

The cluster in the salinity figure in recent years is likely capturing the highly variable conditions due to stratification and fresh pulse that occurred. However, the MAE is 0.004 - 0.002 in many of those cases.

Temperature Maps

# Plot 10 high-error spatial maps
# Reproject bathy
# bathy_utm <- terra::project(bathy, diff_rast)
#bathy_utm <- terra::project(bathy, terra::crs(diff_rast))
# Reproject NES 
us.proj <- terra::project(us.vect, diff_rast)
#pdf("Fishbot_20v10m_Diff_Daily_Temp.pdf", width = 11, height = 8.5) 
#par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(2.5, 2.5, 6, 1), oma = c(0, 0, 2, 0))
for (row in 1:nrow(top_error_days)) {
  idx <- top_error_days$Layer_Index[row]
  day_name <- top_error_days$Day[row]
  current_rmse <- round(top_error_days$RMSE[row], 3)
  current_mae <- round(top_error_days$MAE[row], 3)
  current_layer <- diff_rast[[idx]]
  layer_range <- terra::minmax(current_layer)
  max_diff <- round(max(abs(layer_range)),3)
  # plot
  terra::plot(diff_rast[[idx]], 
             # main = paste0(day_name, "\n(RMSE: ", current_rmse, ")"), 
              type = 'continuous',
             # range = c(-1.5, 1.5), 
              col = hcl.colors(21, "RdBu", rev = TRUE))
  terra::contour(bathy_utm, levels = c(-50,-100, -200, -500),
                 add = TRUE, col = 'grey')
  title(main = paste0(day_name, '\n(RMSE:', current_rmse, ')', 
                      '\n(MAE:', current_mae, ')',
                      '\n(Max Diff:', max_diff, ')'), 
        adj = 0, line = 0.55)
 # terra::plot(us.proj, add = TRUE, col = 'grey90', border = 'gray40')
}
